title: SynRen for Renal Safety Prioritization in Drug Discovery
content: Drug-induced kidney injury presents a persistent challenge in early drug discovery because researchers must connect molecular predictions with exposure, biological context, and experimental priorities. SynRen addresses this task through an AI/ML agent that integrates compound processing, renal prediction, predicted absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) context, compound review, and reporting. We argue that this integration makes a predictive model more useful within the day-to-day work of molecular screening. SynRen’s renal model was developed using a curated 316-compound dataset, comprising 251 development compounds and 65 internal test compounds. Training and internal-test areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) were 0.9998 and 0.7381, respectively. Retrospective external validation achieved AUROC 0.8085 and sensitivity of 90.2% among 81 successfully processed compounds from 83 submitted structures. A separate demonstration generated renal scores for 1,000 compounds and predicted ADMET context for 250 selected compounds, demonstrating execution across a larger library. These completed evaluations support SynRen’s renal screening capability in the assessed populations and its ability to organize a compound screening workflow. This Viewpoint examines how an agent connects renal prediction with accessible compound review and a documented basis for experimental follow-up. SynRen brings these functions into a shared research process in which the researcher directs the objective and interprets the evidence.
